prompts.title: Recent Form: Wins, Draws, Losses
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 motion brief for a recent-form comparison. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles; all other type sits above it. Palette: GoatLab charcoal #101412 background, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for Lille OSC, slate #8ca6bf for Galatasaray SK. Editorial variant, priority: kinetic typography only, no axes, no counts, no sample claims. Open on a charcoal field with a lime vertical rhythm line pulsing like a heartbeat. Spanish team labels “Lille OSC” and “Galatasaray SK” enter from opposite edges and lock into a centred stack. Spanish words “Victorias”, “Empates” and “Derrotas” snap in one by one on a three-beat rhythm, each briefly enlarging then settling; a thin lime underline sweeps under the active word. Add restrained grain and a slow push-in. Hold on the full typographic stack, then a lime wipe transition clears the frame. Statistical variant: grouped count bars on a shared zero baseline, three categories in Spanish: “Victorias”, “Empates”, “Derrotas”. Each category has two bars, lime for Lille OSC and slate for Galatasaray SK. Bar lengths resolve from {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}, {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}} and {{away.losses}}, with units “partidos”. Common scale is computed by the renderer across all six bars. Legend sits top centre; a small Spanish sample badge below the chart reads “muestra: {{home.n}} partidos” and “muestra: {{away.n}} partidos”, and a source/sample annotation in slate uses the catalog source and sampleSize, explicitly showing whether the samples are equal or unequal. Entry: category labels fade up, then bars grow from the baseline with staggered timing; value labels count up and settle. Main comparison: paired bars per category; emphasis lands on the largest lime-versus-slate contrast, with the other bars dimmed to warm white. Camera: slow push-in, no rotation. Transition: lime wipe from lower left. Exit: bars retract to baseline, labels slide down behind the subtitle-safe lower quarter, leaving charcoal.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 motion brief for goals for and against. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Palette: GoatLab charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. Editorial variant, priority: illustrative football pitch, no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. A stylised charcoal pitch drawn in thin warm-white lines tilts into frame; two generic ball paths animate as abstract motion trails, lime from the Lille OSC half and slate from the Galatasaray SK half. They curl toward opposite goals but stop before any specific action, avoiding invented shots or scorelines. Spanish labels “Goles a favor” and “Goles en contra” crossfade into the centre, with team names in small caps. The pitch slowly drifts upward; trails loop once with a soft lime glow, then settle. Transition: a quick ball-swish motion blur wipes to the statistical variant. Statistical variant: horizontal paired bars for both teams on a shared zero baseline. Two rows: “Lille OSC” and “Galatasaray SK”; each row has two bars, lime “A favor” and slate “En contra”. Bar lengths resolve from {{home.gf}}, {{home.ga}}, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}}, with units “goles”. Common scale is computed by the renderer across all four bars. Value labels sit at bar ends; Spanish legend top right. A sample badge under each team reads “muestra: {{home.n}} partidos” and “muestra: {{away.n}} partidos”, and a source/sample line in slate uses the catalog source and sampleSize. Entry: rows wipe in from left, bars extend from the zero baseline with slight overshoot, value labels count up. Main comparison: paired bars per team; emphasis uses a warm-white halo on the longer bar in each pair, while the shorter bar dims. No goal difference is calculated or stated. Camera: gentle vertical drift with a slight push-in. Transition: lime edge wipe. Exit: bars retract to baseline, pitch lines fade, all motion clears the subtitle-safe lower quarter.

prompts.title: Clean Sheets: Counts and Sample
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 motion brief for clean sheets. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Palette: GoatLab charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. Editorial variant, priority: defensive energy with a stylised shield, no statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented saves. Open on charcoal with a faint warm-white penalty-area outline. Two shields materialise: a lime shield for Lille OSC and a slate shield for Galatasaray SK, each with a small Spanish team label. Abstract defensive pressure lines strike the shields and dissolve into particles; the shields pulse but never crack. Spanish words “Arcos en cero” lock across the centre with a lime strike-through that becomes a protective bar. Slow camera push-in; grain and vignette keep it premium. Transition: a shield-edge wipe with a metallic click feel. Statistical variant: compare clean-sheet counts and sample sizes without converting counts into rates. Use two large horizontal count bars on a shared zero baseline, one lime for Lille OSC and one slate for Galatasaray SK. Spanish category label “Arcos en cero”; unit “partidos”. Bar lengths resolve from {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}. Common scale is computed by the renderer across both count bars. At each bar end, a compact Spanish sample chip reads “muestra: {{home.n}} partidos” and “muestra: {{away.n}} partidos”; a source/sample annotation in slate uses the catalog source and sampleSize. Entry: shields shrink into bar ends, then bars extend from the baseline; sample chips slide in after the bars settle. Main comparison: count bars side by side with sample chips attached, so viewers see counts and sample size together. Emphasis: warm-white keyline around the leading count bar, with no rate conversion. Camera: slow top-to-bottom drift and slight push-in. Transition: lime sweep. Exit: bars retract, shields reform briefly, then everything fades above the subtitle-safe lower quarter.
